capabilities.text: Hold the beam on a pivot anywhere along it
Hold the beam on two supports, A and B
Hold the beam from a wall with a cable at 15° to 75° (a hanging sign)
Hold the beam from a wall with no cable (a cantilever)
Set the beam's length, drawn to scale
Measure the beam in m or cm
Give the beam its own weight or mass at its middle, or make it light
Put up to six loads on the beam
Draw each load as a block or a ball
Hang each load from the beam or rest it on top
Make a load a force arrow pointing down or up
Place each load where you want along the beam
Give the loads in N, or as masses in kg or g
Use g = 9.8, 9.81 or 10 N/kg for masses
capabilities.note: passes on load_units alone; checked by hand that g = 10 changes the worked render

capabilities.text: Label each load with its value, your own text, a blank line, or nothing
Label each distance with its value, your own text, a blank line, or nothing
Mark the distances from the pivot, support A or the wall
Mark the beam's whole length
Draw a weight arrow down from every object
Draw the forces holding the beam up
capabilities.note: ours draws the support forces on the answer key only (show_reactions needs Show answers)

capabilities.text: Work out the torques, support forces or cable tension step by step
Balance the beam by solving for any one load
Mirror the figure so the wall is on the right
Draw in color for slides, or black and white
Set each load's drawn size
capabilities.note: the page's 'Balanced with this value' button is already cap-07b
